isc_api_security._note: Lab 51 policy. Checked 2026-11 against developer.sailpoint.com (Authentication, Authorization) and documentation.sailpoint.com (Managing API Keys and Personal Access Tokens, User Level Permissions, User Level Access Matrix, Configuring Multifactor Authentication, Configuring Pass-Through Authentication, Configuring ... as a Service Provider, Configuring Session Lengths). Verified: token endpoint https://[tenant].api.identitynow.com/oauth/token and authorize endpoint https://[tenant].login.sailpoint.com/oauth/authorize; grant types CLIENT_CREDENTIALS, AUTHORIZATION_CODE, REFRESH_TOKEN; client credentials tokens carry no user context and most admin APIs answer 403 to them; API keys fail on role, entitlement and identity search when Data Segmentation is on; PATs act with the owner's user levels; up to 10 PATs per user, default expiry 6 months, blank = no expiry; sp:scopes:default and sp:scopes:all; the client secret is shown once; user levels, the incompatible combinations and the Sub-Admin governance-group scoping; elevated users (any level with the Admin menu) need a TOTP authenticator; SSO bypass with ?prompt=true for elevated users; PTA sources Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, OpenLDAP, SunOne; default sessions 12 hours maximum and 15 minutes idle. Simplified training values (not SailPoint numbers): which tasks need a user context, the narrow scope names other than idn:access-request:manage and idn:access-profile:read (they follow SailPoint's idn:<resource>:read|manage pattern but check each endpoint's specification), the approved secret stores, the 2-emergency-admin rule and the session limits the company sets itself.

integration_types.service: an unattended service integration with no person signed in
integration_types.web_app: a web application that calls the API on behalf of the user signed in to it

sign_in_methods.USERNAME_PASSWORD: users sign in with an ISC user name and password
sign_in_methods.PASS_THROUGH: users sign in with the password of a directory source (pass-through authentication)
sign_in_methods.MFA: users sign in and then confirm with a multifactor authentication method

concepts.personal access token: A client ID and secret that a user creates for scripts; tokens issued from it carry that user's identity and user levels.
concepts.API client: An OAuth 2.0 client an admin creates under Security Settings > API Management for an application or service integration.
concepts.client credentials grant: An OAuth 2.0 flow where a service trades its client ID and secret for a token that has no user context.
concepts.authorization code grant: An OAuth 2.0 flow where a web app sends the user to sign in and receives a token that acts as that user.
concepts.scope: A label on a token or client that limits which endpoints it can call, always inside what the user level allows.
concepts.user level: A set of admin permissions in ISC, such as Admin, Source Admin or Helpdesk; levels add up when combined.
concepts.Sub-Admin: A Source or Role user level that only works on sources tied to the governance groups the person belongs to.
concepts.emergency bypass: Signing in with ?prompt=true to skip the SSO identity provider, allowed for elevated users when the IdP is down.
